correctness.rationale: A two-sided characterization of general-position subsets of \(K_m\times K_n\) \(m,n\ge3\) by row/column subsets, partial permutations and three- or four-corner rectangles follows from the induced-\(P_3\) criterion. All configuration types are enumerated without overlap after correcting empty and singleton sets. One-vertex extension checks classify all maximal configurations. The coefficients for \(K_3\times K_n\) obey exact cubic and factored inequalities yielding unimodality precisely for \(3\le n\le10\) or \(n\ge18\). A direct graph-level enumeration over 1,151,488 subsets in five profiles and integer verification for 276 facet profiles and \(3\le n\le300\) reproduced the formulas, with the infinite assertion resting on the written proof.

originality.rationale: The direct-product paper by Di Stefano et al. (arXiv:2306.09965, section 5.4) already proves the scalar lower general-position number and exhibits clique, layer, and rectangle examples. The present claim does not reassert those known results as novel; it proves the exhaustive two-parameter complete all-set and inclusion-maximal-set enumerators and a new exact loss-and-recovery window for unimodality. The 2024 full-text general-position-polynomial paper studies Cartesian rather than categorical products and does not give these coefficients. Semantic index and textual searches yielded no dominating/equivalent counting theorem, subject to genuine residual bibliographic risk.
residual_risks: An equivalent induced-cluster-subgraph enumeration of the complement of a rook graph could be indexed under unrelated terminology.
The 2018 structural-characterization paper was only compared through its primary abstract, not its full text; it could contain subsidiary product enumerations.
Priority is a best-knowledge literature comparison, not a theorem of uniqueness or a substitute for independent expert review.

value.rationale: The complete counting polynomial answers a natural two-parameter enumeration problem, and the maximal-set enumerator determines the full facet-size spectrum, unique pure case \(K_4\times K_4\), and unbounded missing cardinality gaps on \(K_3\times K_n\). The exact finite band \(11\le n\le17\) of nonunimodality followed by restoration at \(n\ge18\) is a sharp coefficient-shape phenomenon motivated by existing research on graph general-position polynomials; neither a known scalar minimum nor trivial relabeling delivers it.
